finding.text: On a wide screen the stuck tab strip doesn't cover the full width. The strip sits beside the title (`flex: 1 1 24em`), so when the title scrolls away, the content scrolls through the empty spot to its left: the properties card shows at the top-left in shots/page-1920-scrolled.png (x 310–460, y 0–77), and so does the dark code block in shots/tabs-1920-scrolled.png. Ask 2, "on a wide screen, the tab row sticks", is only half met.

The code block on core/Page now runs to the right screen edge at 390 (shots/page-390-top.png, band 6, x 16–390), and so does the page.jsonl block in shots/page-390-scrolled.png. In shots/before-page-390-top.png it stopped 28px short. The smaller `--gutter-x` probably dropped the right inset of the wide blocks. (layout 5, spacing)

The page title and the content no longer share a left edge on a phone. "Task queue" starts at about x 8, but its cards start at x 16 (shots/queue-390-top.png, bands 3–4). On /framework/ai/ at 400, layout.json `left_stack.h1` is 12, while the content starts at 24. (layout, one left edge)
At 1920 the AI queue page is too short to scroll, so shots/queue-1920-scrolled.png looks the same as -top. Nothing shows the AI tab strip sticking on a wide screen.

On /framework/ai/ at 400, the filter chips (Ready to merge … Processes) wrap onto 3 rows (shots/…-framework-ai/400.png, band 2). They are a chip row, not a `.tab-bar` (layout.json `tab_rows` 0), so the brief's "every tab row" may not cover them. Still, they read as tabs and take 3 lines.
